open_roleplay.label: opens by telling the model to play a part: Act as, Behave like, Take on

open_statement.label: opens with a plain statement: You <verb>, Your <noun>

open_risky.label: opens with You have / believe / want / tend to, When

chat_words.label: chat-frame words (user, assistant, AI, your responses), not in an AI role

softened.label: the role softened, whitewashed or excused (judged)

hedge_words.label: hedge words (appropriate, healthy, sometimes, may, tends to ...)

observer_words.label: the rubric's observer words (navigating, individuals, demonstrate ...)

observer_register.label: an outsider's register, not the role's own words (judged)

off_role.label: a different role, a trait, or too narrow a part (judged)

invented_motive.label: a motive the description does not give, as fact (judged)

dashes.label: uses a dash (the rubric asks for commas)

echo_description.label: repeats 5 or more words in a row of the description

copied_example.label: repeats 7 or more words in a row of a template example

q_persona.label: addresses the person answering (second person, no first-person asker)

q_shape_situation.label: puts the person in a situation (judged)

q_first_person.label: asker speaks in the first person

q_shape_other_kinds.label: how-to, facts, bare task or general opinion (judged)

q_factual.label: opens as a request for facts

q_yes_no.label: can be answered in full with yes or no (judged)

q_two_option.label: spells out two courses of action (judged)

q_one_answer.label: one right or one safe answer (judged)

q_outside_world.label: not set in the role's world (judged)

q_performs.label: asks the person to perform or describe the role (judged)

q_chat_words.label: mentions an AI, an assistant or a user, not in an AI role
